# Startup compatibility observations

Reference: unchanged Gophish Community Edition 0.12.1, commit 95618469799295e2c0fec980805a2dfbb818816b. The observations call the unchanged exported config.LoadConfig and util.CheckAndCreateSSL functions. config.json was captured on 2026-10-18 and includes the original TestLoadConfig valid example plus defaults, duplicate/case-folded fields, nested merges, nulls, unknown fields, invalid types and trailing JSON. Expected values come from Go rather than the Rust decoder. Nil versus empty Go slices are equivalent for these configuration policies; the regression normalizes only that distinction.

go-admin.crt and go-admin.key are a synthetic P-384 certificate and SEC1 EC private key produced by Go's unchanged certificate helper. That legacy certificate has no SAN, so its one loopback compatibility request explicitly skips identity validation. go-rsa.crt and go-rsa.key were generated by the capture tool using Go's crypto/x509 and crypto/rsa, with a loopback SAN and PKCS#1 private key. Their TLS test uses only that explicit trusted root, preserving chain and hostname checks without imposing native OS policy on the historical ten-year fixture. Newly generated production certificates are tested separately with the native verifier. All private keys here are deliberately public synthetic fixtures and must never be used for an installation.

To extend the corpus, capture independent observations into a new directory, review them, and copy only deliberately added fixtures; do not regenerate existing expectations silently. manifest.json records the reviewed bytes.

cli.json records observations from the unchanged Go executable. It preserves observed exits, output-stream presence and whether parsing reached configuration loading; only the temporary missing-config filename is normalized. The negative boolean alias is --no-disable-mailer; explicit values such as --disable-mailer=false are rejected. Version output precedes a later unknown flag, whereas help does not hide unknown flags.
